title.zh: 卷七 本紀第七 前廢帝
title.raw: 卷七 本紀第七 前廢帝 Volume 7 Annals 7: Emperor Fei I

sentences.zh: 前廢帝諱子業，小字法師，孝武帝長子也。

translations.literal: The Former Deposed Emperor, taboo name Ziye, childhood name Fashi, was Emperor Xiaowu's eldest son.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Fei I, whose personal name was Ziye and whose childhood name was Fashi, was the eldest son of Emperor Xiaowu.

sentences.zh: 元嘉二十六年正月甲申生。

translations.literal: He was born on jiazi day in the first month of the twenty-sixth year of Yuanjia.
translations.idiomatic: He was born on the jiazi day of the first month in the twenty-sixth year of Yuanjia.

sentences.zh: 世祖鎮尋陽，子業留京邑。

translations.literal: When the Emperor garrisoned Xunyang, Ziye remained in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: While the Emperor was posted at Xunyang, Ziye stayed behind in the capital.

sentences.zh: 三十年，世祖入伐元凶，被囚侍中下省，將見害者數矣，卒得無恙。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year, when the Emperor entered the capital to attack the Assassin Prince, he was imprisoned in the Attendant-Censorate's lower bureau; several times he was about to be killed, but in the end escaped unharmed.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirtieth year, when the Emperor marched in to punish the Assassin Prince, Ziye was held in the lower bureau of the Attendant-Censorate. He was nearly killed more than once before he finally came through unscathed.

sentences.zh: 世祖踐阼，立為皇太子。

translations.literal: When the Emperor ascended the throne, he was installed as crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: After the Emperor took the throne, Ziye was installed as crown prince.

sentences.zh: 始未之東宮，中庶子、二率並入直永福省。

translations.literal: At first he had not yet gone to the Eastern Palace; the Palace Prefect and the two commandants all entered duty at Yongfu Palace.
translations.idiomatic: At first he had not yet moved into the Eastern Palace; the Palace Prefect and the two guard commandants all served on duty at Yongfu Palace.

sentences.zh: 大明二年，出居東宮。

translations.literal: In the second year of Daming he moved out to reside in the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Daming he took up residence in the Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: [1]四年，講孝經於崇正殿。

translations.literal: [1] In the fourth year he lectured on the Classic of Filial Piety in Chongzheng Hall.
translations.idiomatic: [1] In the fourth year he lectured on the Classic of Filial Piety in Chongzheng Hall.

sentences.zh: 七年，加元服。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he received the capping ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he underwent the capping ceremony.

sentences.zh: 八年閏五月庚申，世祖崩，其日，太子即皇帝位。

translations.literal: On gengshen day in the intercalary fifth month of the eighth year, the Emperor died; that same day the crown prince assumed the imperial position.
translations.idiomatic: On the gengshen day of the intercalary fifth month in the eighth year, the Emperor died; that same day the crown prince ascended the throne.

sentences.zh: 大赦天下。

translations.literal: A general amnesty was proclaimed throughout the empire.
translations.idiomatic: A general amnesty was proclaimed throughout the empire.

sentences.zh: 太宰江夏王義恭解尚書令，加中書監，驃騎大將軍柳元景加尚書令。

translations.literal: Grand Tutor Prince Jiangxia of Yixia was relieved of Director of the Masters of Writing and given the additional post of Supervisor of the Masters of Writing. General-in-Chief Who Runs Fast Liu Yuanjing was given the additional post of Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Tutor Prince Jiangxia of Yixia stepped down as Director of the Masters of Writing and was made Supervisor of the Masters of Writing instead. General-in-Chief Who Runs Fast Liu Yuanjing was appointed Director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 甲子，置錄尚書，太宰江夏王義恭錄尚書事。

translations.literal: On jiazi day the office of Recorder of the Masters of Writing was established; Grand Tutor Prince Jiangxia of Yixia was made Recorder of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiazi day the post of Recorder of the Masters of Writing was created, and Grand Tutor Prince Jiangxia of Yixia was appointed to it.

sentences.zh: 驃騎大將軍柳元景加開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: General-in-Chief Who Runs Fast Liu Yuanjing was given the additional title of Bearer of the Staff with Equal Protocol to a Three-Division Office.
translations.idiomatic: General-in-Chief Who Runs Fast Liu Yuanjing was granted the Staff of Authority with protocol equal to a three-division office.

sentences.zh: 丹陽尹永嘉王子仁為南豫州刺史。

translations.literal: Director of Danyang Yin Prince Yongjia of Yongxing was made Inspector of Southern Yuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yongjia of Yongxing, who was serving as Director of Danyang, was appointed Inspector of Southern Yuzhou.

translations.literal: [2] Here it reads Southern Yuzhou; in Prince Ziren's biography the post is Southern Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: [Note 2: The text here reads Southern Yuzhou, but Prince Ziren's biography gives the appointment as Southern Yanzhou.]

sentences.zh: 六月辛未，詔曰：「朕以眇身，夙紹洪業，敬御天威，欽對靈命。

translations.literal: On xinwei day in the sixth month an edict said: "I, with my slight person, have early inherited the great enterprise, respectfully bearing Heaven's majesty and reverently facing the numinous mandate.
translations.idiomatic: On the xinwei day of the sixth month an edict said: "I, slight in person, have early inherited the great enterprise, reverently bearing Heaven's majesty and facing the numinous mandate.

sentences.zh: 仰遵凝緒，日鑒前圖，實可以拱默守成，詒風長世。

translations.literal: Looking up to follow the solidified thread of succession, daily taking the former chart as mirror, truly one could fold the arms in silence and guard the accomplishment, passing down the style for generations.
translations.idiomatic: Upholding the settled line of succession and taking past models as my daily mirror, I might truly have folded my arms in silence, guarded what was won, and let good governance endure for generations.

sentences.zh: 而寶位告始，萬宇改屬，惟德弗明，昧于大道。

translations.literal: Yet when the precious position was first announced, the myriad realms changed their allegiance; virtue alone is not bright, and I am obscure regarding the great Way.
translations.idiomatic: Yet no sooner had the throne been announced than the realm changed hands; my virtue is not yet clear, and I remain blind to the great Way.

sentences.zh: 思宣睿範，引茲簡恤，可具詢執事，詳訪民隱。

translations.literal: I wish to spread the enlightened model and extend this simplified compassion; let the responsible officials be fully consulted and the people's hardships carefully investigated.
translations.idiomatic: I wish to proclaim an enlightened standard and extend this measure of relief: let every responsible office be consulted and the people's hardships thoroughly investigated.

sentences.zh: 凡曲令密文，繁而傷治，[3]關市僦稅，事施一時，而姦吏舞文，妄興威福，加以氣緯舛互，[4]偏頗滋甚。

translations.literal: All crooked orders and secret statutes, elaborate and harmful to governance, [3] market tolls and lease taxes imposed for a time only—yet corrupt clerks wield documents and recklessly raise authority and blessing, and moreover the qi configurations cross and conflict, [4] partiality grows ever worse.
translations.idiomatic: Every crooked statute and secret regulation that is elaborate yet injures good governance, [3] every market toll and transit tax imposed only for a season—yet corrupt clerks twist the written law and recklessly wield power, while the qi configurations clash and conflict [4] and partiality grows worse by the day.

sentences.zh: 宜其寬傜輕憲，以救民切。

translations.literal: It is fitting to broaden corvée and lighten punishments, to relieve the people's urgent distress.
translations.idiomatic: Corvée should be eased and penalties lightened to relieve the people's urgent distress.

sentences.zh: 御府諸署，事不須廣，雕文篆刻，無施於今。

translations.literal: The various offices of the Imperial Household need not be broad; carved writing and seal engraving have no place in the present.
translations.idiomatic: The various offices of the Imperial Household need not be numerous; carved ornament and seal engraving have no place today.

sentences.zh: 悉宜并省，以酬氓願。

translations.literal: All should be merged and reduced, to answer the common people's wish.
translations.idiomatic: They should all be consolidated and cut back to answer the people's wish.

sentences.zh: 藩王貿貨，壹皆禁斷。

translations.literal: Princely trade in goods is entirely forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: Trade in goods by imperial princes is forbidden altogether.

sentences.zh: 外便具條以聞。

translations.literal: Let the outer offices prepare detailed entries and report.
translations.idiomatic: Let the outer offices prepare detailed reports and submit them.

sentences.zh: 」戊寅，以豫州之淮南郡復為南梁郡，復分宣城還置淮南郡。

translations.literal: " On wuyin day Huainan commandery in Yuzhou was restored as Southern Liang commandery; Xuancheng was again divided off to re-establish Huainan commandery.
translations.idiomatic: " On the wuyin day Huainan commandery in Yuzhou was restored as Southern Liang commandery, and Xuancheng was split off again to re-establish Huainan commandery.

sentences.zh: 庚辰，以南海太守袁曇遠為廣州刺史。

translations.literal: On gengchen day Yuan Tanyuan, Administrator of Nanhai, was made Inspector of Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On the gengchen day Yuan Tanyuan, Administrator of Nanhai, was appointed Inspector of Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 秋七月己亥，鎮軍將軍、雍州刺史晉安王子勛改為江州刺史，中護軍宗慤為安西將軍、雍州刺史，鎮北將軍、徐州刺史湘東王彧為護軍將軍，中軍將軍義陽王昶為征北將軍、徐州刺史。

translations.literal: On jihai day in the seventh month of autumn, General Who Pacifies the Army and Inspector of Yong Prince Jin'an of Jin'an was changed to Inspector of Jiangzhou; Colonel of the Guard Zong Que was made General Who Pacifies the West and Inspector of Yong; General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Xuzhou Prince Xiangdong of Xiangdong was made General Who Protects the Army; General of the Center Prince Yiyang of Yiyang was made General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On the jihai day of the seventh month, General Who Pacifies the Army and Inspector of Yong Prince Jin'an of Jin'an was reassigned as Inspector of Jiangzhou; Colonel of the Guard Zong Que became General Who Pacifies the West and Inspector of Yong; General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Xuzhou Prince Xiangdong of Xiangdong was made General Who Protects the Army; and General of the Center Prince Yiyang of Yiyang was appointed General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 庚戌，婆皇國遣使獻方物。

translations.literal: On gengxu day the Po Huang state sent envoys presenting local products.
translations.idiomatic: On the gengxu day the kingdom of Po Huang sent envoys bearing tribute goods.

sentences.zh: 崇皇太后曰太皇太后，皇后曰皇太后。

translations.literal: The Honored Empress Dowager was styled Grand Empress Dowager; the empress was styled Empress Dowager.
translations.idiomatic: The Honored Empress Dowager was elevated to Grand Empress Dowager, and the empress was styled Empress Dowager.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，罷南北二馳道。

translations.literal: On yimao day the northern and southern expressways were abolished.
translations.idiomatic: On the yimao day the northern and southern imperial expressways were abolished.

sentences.zh: 孝建以來所改制度，還依元嘉。

translations.literal: Institutions changed since Xiaojian were restored according to Yuanjia.
translations.idiomatic: Institutions altered since the Xiaojian era were restored to the Yuanjia standard.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，追崇獻妃為獻皇后。

translations.literal: On bingchen day the late Consort Xian was posthumously honored as Empress Xian.
translations.idiomatic: On the bingchen day the late Consort Xian was posthumously honored as Empress Xian.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，撫軍將軍、南徐州刺史新安王子鸞解領司徒。

translations.literal: On yichou day General Who Pacifies the Army and Inspector of Southern Xuzhou Prince Xin'an of Xin'an was relieved of his concurrent post as Minister.
translations.idiomatic: On the yichou day General Who Pacifies the Army and Inspector of Southern Xuzhou Prince Xin'an of Xin'an relinquished his concurrent office as Minister.

sentences.zh: 八月丁卯，領軍將軍王玄謨為鎮北將軍、青冀二州刺史。

translations.literal: In the eighth month on dingmao day Colonel of the Garrison Wang Xuemo was made General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Qing and Ji.
translations.idiomatic: On the dingmao day of the eighth month Colonel of the Garrison Wang Xuemo was appointed General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Qing and Ji.

sentences.zh: [5]己巳，以青、冀二州刺史蕭惠開為益州刺史。

translations.literal: [5] On jisi day Xiao Huikai, Inspector of Qing and Ji, was made Inspector of Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: [5] On the jisi day Xiao Huikai, Inspector of Qing and Ji, was appointed Inspector of Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 己丑，[6]皇太后崩。

translations.literal: [6] On jichou day the Empress Dowager died.
translations.idiomatic: [6] On the jichou day the Empress Dowager died.

sentences.zh: 京師雨水。

translations.literal: In the capital region it rained continuously.
translations.idiomatic: Rain fell without cease in the capital region.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，[7]遣御史與官長隨宜賑卹。

translations.literal: [7] On gengyin day censors were dispatched together with office heads to provide relief as circumstances required.
translations.idiomatic: [7] On the gengyin day censors were sent out with local officials to provide relief wherever it was needed.

sentences.zh: 九月辛丑，護軍將軍湘東王彧為領軍將軍。

translations.literal: In the ninth month on xinchou day General Who Protects the Army Prince Xiangdong of Xiangdong was made Colonel of the Garrison.
translations.idiomatic: On the xinchou day of the ninth month General Who Protects the Army Prince Xiangdong of Xiangdong was appointed Colonel of the Garrison.

sentences.zh: 癸卯，以尚書左僕射劉遵考為特進、右光祿大夫。

translations.literal: On guimao day Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Liu Zunkao was made Special Grand Master and Right Minister of the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: On the guimao day Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Liu Zunkao was promoted to Special Grand Master and Right Minister of the Palace.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，文穆皇后祔葬景寧陵。

translations.literal: On yimao day Empress Wenmu was enshrined beside the Emperor at Jingning Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: On the yimao day Empress Wenmu was enshrined beside the late Emperor at Jingning Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 冬十月甲戌，太常建安王休仁為護軍將軍。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of winter on jiaxu day Minister of Ceremonies Prince Jian'an of Jian'an was made General Who Protects the Army.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiaxu day of the tenth month Minister of Ceremonies Prince Jian'an of Jian'an was appointed General Who Protects the Army.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，輔國將軍宗越為司州刺史。

translations.literal: On wuyin day General Who Assists the State Zong Yue was made Inspector of Sizhou.
translations.idiomatic: On the wuyin day General Who Assists the State Zong Yue was appointed Inspector of Sizhou.

sentences.zh: [8]庚辰，原除揚、南徐州大明七年逋租。

translations.literal: [8] On gengchen day overdue rents from the seventh year of Daming in Yang and Southern Xuzhou were remitted.
translations.idiomatic: [8] On the gengchen day overdue rents from the seventh year of Daming in Yang and Southern Xuzhou were remitted.

sentences.zh: 十二月乙酉，以尚書右僕射顏師伯為尚書僕射。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month on yiyou day Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Yan Shibo was made Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: On the yiyou day of the twelfth month Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Yan Shibo was promoted to Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: [9]壬辰，以王畿諸郡為揚州，以揚州為東揚州。

translations.literal: [9] On renchen day the commanderies of the metropolitan belt were made Yangzhou, and Yangzhou was made Eastern Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: [9] On the renchen day the commanderies of the metropolitan belt were reorganized as Yangzhou, while the former Yangzhou became Eastern Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，以車騎將軍、揚州刺史豫章王子尚為司徒、揚州刺史。

translations.literal: On guisi day General of Chariots and Cavalry and Inspector of Yangzhou Prince Yuzhang of Yuzhang was made Minister and Inspector of Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On the guisi day General of Chariots and Cavalry and Inspector of Yangzhou Prince Yuzhang of Yuzhang was appointed Minister and Inspector of Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 去歲及是歲，東諸郡大旱，甚者米一升數百，京邑亦至百餘，餓死者十有六七。

translations.literal: In the previous year and this year the eastern commanderies suffered great drought; in the worst cases a sheng of grain cost several hundred, and in the capital as much as a hundred-odd; those who starved to death were six or seven out of ten.
translations.idiomatic: In the previous year and this year the eastern commanderies suffered severe drought; in the worst places a sheng of grain cost several hundred cash, and even in the capital more than a hundred. Six or seven out of every ten people starved to death.

sentences.zh: 孝建以來，又立錢署鑄錢，百姓因此盜鑄，錢轉偽小，商貨不行。

translations.literal: Since Xiaojian, money offices were also established to cast coin; because of this the common people illicitly cast as well, the cash grew ever more false and small, and commerce would not circulate.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Xiaojian era mints had been set up to cast coin, and the people responded by counterfeiting in turn until the money grew false and light and trade ceased to circulate.

sentences.zh: 永光元年春正月乙未朔，改元。

translations.literal: In the first month of spring in the first year of Yongguang, on yiwei day, the first day of the month, the era name was changed.
translations.idiomatic: On the yiwei day, the first day of the first month of spring in the first year of Yongguang, the era name was changed.

sentences.zh: 大赦天下。

translations.literal: A general amnesty was proclaimed throughout the empire.
translations.idiomatic: A general amnesty was proclaimed throughout the empire.

sentences.zh: 乙巳，省諸州臺傳。

translations.literal: On yisi day the provincial relay offices were abolished.
translations.idiomatic: On the yisi day the provincial relay offices were abolished.

sentences.zh: 戊午，以領軍將軍湘東王彧為衞將軍、南豫州刺史，護軍將軍建安王休仁為領軍將軍，祕書監山陽王休祐為豫州刺史，左衞將軍桂陽王休範為中護軍，南豫州刺史尋陽王子房為東揚州刺史。

translations.literal: On wuwu day Colonel of the Garrison Prince Xiangdong of Xiangdong was made General of the Guard and Inspector of Southern Yuzhou; General Who Protects the Army Prince Jian'an of Jian'an was made Colonel of the Garrison; Supervisor of the Masters of Writing Prince Shanyang of Shanyang was made Inspector of Yuzhou; Colonel of the Left Guard Prince Guiyang of Guiyang was made Colonel of the Guard; Inspector of Southern Yuzhou Prince Xunyang of Xunyang was made Inspector of Eastern Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On the wuwu day Colonel of the Garrison Prince Xiangdong of Xiangdong became General of the Guard and Inspector of Southern Yuzhou; General Who Protects the Army Prince Jian'an of Jian'an was made Colonel of the Garrison; Supervisor of the Masters of Writing Prince Shanyang of Shanyang was appointed Inspector of Yuzhou; Colonel of the Left Guard Prince Guiyang of Guiyang became Colonel of the Guard; and Inspector of Southern Yuzhou Prince Xunyang of Xunyang was made Inspector of Eastern Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 二月乙丑，減州郡縣田祿之半。

translations.literal: In the second month on yichou day the field salaries of provinces, commanderies, and counties were reduced by half.
translations.idiomatic: On the yichou day of the second month the field-salary allotments of provinces, commanderies, and counties were cut by half.

sentences.zh: [10]庚寅，鑄二銖錢。

translations.literal: [10] On gengyin day two-zhu cash was cast.
translations.idiomatic: [10] On the gengyin day two-zhu cash was cast.

sentences.zh: 三月甲辰，罷臨江郡。

translations.literal: In the third month on jiachen day Linjiang commandery was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiachen day of the third month Linjiang commandery was abolished.

sentences.zh: 五月己亥，割郢州隨郡屬雍州。

translations.literal: In the fifth month on jihai day Suo commandery in Yingzhou was detached and placed under Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On the jihai day of the fifth month Suo commandery in Yingzhou was transferred to Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 丙午，以後軍司馬張牧為交州刺史。

translations.literal: On bingwu day Rear Army Major Zhang Mu was made Inspector of Jiaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: On the bingwu day Rear Army Major Zhang Mu was appointed Inspector of Jiaozhou.

sentences.zh: 六月己巳，左軍長史劉道隆為梁、南秦二州刺史。

translations.literal: In the sixth month on jisi day Left Army Chief Clerk Liu Daolong was made Inspector of Liang and Southern Qin.
translations.idiomatic: On the jisi day of the sixth month Left Army Chief Clerk Liu Daolong was appointed Inspector of Liang and Southern Qin.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，安西將軍、雍州刺史宗慤卒。

translations.literal: On yihai day General Who Pacifies the West and Inspector of Yong Zong Que died.
translations.idiomatic: On the yihai day General Who Pacifies the West and Inspector of Yong Zong Que died.

sentences.zh: 壬午，衞將軍、南豫州刺史湘東王彧改為雍州刺史。

translations.literal: On renwu day General of the Guard and Inspector of Southern Yuzhou Prince Xiangdong of Xiangdong was changed to Inspector of Yong.
translations.idiomatic: On the renwu day General of the Guard and Inspector of Southern Yuzhou Prince Xiangdong of Xiangdong was reassigned as Inspector of Yong.

sentences.zh: [11]尚書令、驃騎大將軍柳元景加南豫州刺史。

translations.literal: [11] Director of the Masters of Writing and General-in-Chief Who Runs Fast Liu Yuanjing was given the additional post of Inspector of Southern Yuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: [11] Director of the Masters of Writing and General-in-Chief Who Runs Fast Liu Yuanjing was also made Inspector of Southern Yuzhou.

sentences.zh: 秋八月辛酉，越騎校尉戴法興有罪，賜死。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of autumn on xinyou day Colonel of the Swift Cavalry Dai Faxing committed an offense and was ordered to die.
translations.idiomatic: On the xinyou day of the eighth month Colonel of the Swift Cavalry Dai Faxing was found guilty and ordered to take his own life.

sentences.zh: 庚午，以尚書僕射顏師伯為尚書左僕射，[12]吏部尚書王景文為尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: On gengwu day Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Yan Shibo was made Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing; [12] Director of the Ministry of Personnel Wang Jingwen was made Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: On the gengwu day Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Yan Shibo was promoted to Left Vice Director; [12] Director of the Ministry of Personnel Wang Jingwen was made Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 癸酉，帝自率宿衞兵，誅太宰江夏王義恭、尚書令驃騎大將軍柳元景、尚書左僕射顏師伯、[13]廷尉劉德願。

translations.literal: On guiyou day the Emperor personally led the palace guard troops and executed Grand Tutor Prince Jiangxia of Yixia, Director of the Masters of Writing and General-in-Chief Who Runs Fast Liu Yuanjing, Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Yan Shibo, [13] and Commandant of Justice Liu Deyuan.
translations.idiomatic: On the guiyou day the Emperor personally led the palace guards and put to death Grand Tutor Prince Jiangxia of Yixia, Director of the Masters of Writing and General-in-Chief Who Runs Fast Liu Yuanjing, Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Yan Shibo, [13] and Commandant of Justice Liu Deyuan.

sentences.zh: 改元為景和元年。

translations.literal: The era name was changed to the first year of Jinghe.
translations.idiomatic: The era name was changed to Jinghe.

sentences.zh: 文武賜位二等。

translations.literal: Civil and military officials were granted two ranks in nobility.
translations.idiomatic: Civil and military officials were promoted two ranks in nobility.

sentences.zh: 以領軍將軍建安王休仁為安西將軍、雍州刺史，衞將軍湘東王彧還為南豫州刺史。

translations.literal: Colonel of the Garrison Prince Jian'an of Jian'an was made General Who Pacifies the West and Inspector of Yong; General of the Guard Prince Xiangdong of Xiangdong returned as Inspector of Southern Yuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Colonel of the Garrison Prince Jian'an of Jian'an was appointed General Who Pacifies the West and Inspector of Yong, and General of the Guard Prince Xiangdong of Xiangdong returned to his post as Inspector of Southern Yuzhou.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，司徒、揚州刺史豫章王子尚領尚書令，射聲校尉沈文秀為青州刺史，左軍司馬崔道固為冀州刺史。

translations.literal: On jiaxu day Minister and Inspector of Yangzhou Prince Yuzhang of Yuzhang took charge of Director of the Masters of Writing; Colonel of the Archers Shen Wenxiu was made Inspector of Qingzhou; Left Army Major Cui Daogu was made Inspector of Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiaxu day Minister and Inspector of Yangzhou Prince Yuzhang of Yuzhang assumed the directorship of the Masters of Writing; Colonel of the Archers Shen Wenxiu was appointed Inspector of Qingzhou; and Left Army Major Cui Daogu was made Inspector of Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，詔曰：「昔凝神佇逸，磻溪讚道，湛慮思才，傅巖毗化。

translations.literal: On yihai day an edict said: "In antiquity, concentrating the spirit and waiting in stillness, Panxi praised the Way; deep thought pondering talent, Fuyan assisted in transformation.
translations.idiomatic: On the yihai day an edict said: "In antiquity, when one concentrated the spirit and waited in stillness, Panxi praised the Way; when one pondered talent in deep thought, Fuyan aided in transformation.

sentences.zh: 朕位御三極，風澄萬宇，資鈇電斷，正卯斯戮。

translations.literal: I occupy the three extremities, the winds are clear throughout the myriad realms; relying on the axe and lightning for judgment, at the hour of mao the punishments are carried out.
translations.idiomatic: I occupy the throne at the three extremities, and the winds are clear throughout the realm; relying on the axe of judgment and the lightning of authority, at the hour of mao I carry out punishment.

sentences.zh: 思所以仰宣遺烈，俯弘景祚，每結夢庖鼎，瞻言板築，有劬日昃，無忘昧旦。

translations.literal: Thinking how to look up and proclaim the legacy left behind, look down and extend the splendid fortune—each night I dream of the ding cauldron, each word recalls the board for building; from morning to evening there is toil, and I do not forget the hour before dawn.
translations.idiomatic: I mean to look up and proclaim the legacy I have received and look down to extend the dynasty's fortune; night after night I dream of the ding cauldron, and every word recalls the builder's plank—my toil runs from dawn to dusk, and I do not forget the hour before dawn.

sentences.zh: 可甄訪郡國，招聘閭部：其有孝性忠節，幽居遯棲，信誠義行，廉正表俗，文敏博識，幹事治民，務加旌舉，隨才引擢。

translations.literal: Let commanderies and states be examined and recruited from within the districts: those with filial conduct and loyal integrity, dwelling in seclusion in remote places, with trustworthiness, sincerity, righteous conduct, integrity upright and exemplary for custom, literary refinement and broad knowledge, able in affairs and governing the people—give them all increased commendation and promote them according to their talents.
translations.idiomatic: Let every commandery and state be searched and talent recruited from the districts: anyone showing filial piety and loyal integrity, living in seclusion far from office, demonstrating trustworthiness, sincerity, and righteous conduct, upright integrity that sets an example for the people, literary refinement and broad learning, or skill in affairs and governance—such persons should be commended and promoted according to their abilities.

sentences.zh: 庶官克順，彝倫咸叙。

translations.literal: Then the officials will be able to comply, and the norms will all be ordered.
translations.idiomatic: Then officials will perform their duties and the moral order will be restored.

sentences.zh: 主者精加詳括，稱朕意焉。

translations.literal: Those in charge should carefully add detailed review, declaring my intent.
translations.idiomatic: The responsible offices should examine the matter carefully and report in accord with my intent.

sentences.zh: 」以始興公沈慶之為太尉，鎮北將軍、青冀二州刺史王玄謨為領軍將軍。

translations.literal: " Duke of Shixing Shen Qingzhi was made Grand Commandant; General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Qing and Ji Wang Xuemo was made Colonel of the Garrison.
translations.idiomatic: " Duke of Shixing Shen Qingzhi was appointed Grand Commandant, and General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Qing and Ji Wang Xuemo was made Colonel of the Garrison.

sentences.zh: 庚辰，以石頭城為長樂宮，東府城為未央宮。

translations.literal: On gengchen day Stone City was made Everlasting Joy Palace, and the Eastern Headquarters was made Weiyang Palace.
translations.idiomatic: On the gengchen day Stone City was renamed Everlasting Joy Palace and the Eastern Headquarters was renamed Weiyang Palace.

sentences.zh: 罷東揚州并揚州。

translations.literal: Eastern Yangzhou was abolished and merged into Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Yangzhou was abolished and merged back into Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 甲申，以北邸為建章宮，南第為長楊宮。

translations.literal: On jiashen day the northern residence was made Jianzhang Palace and the southern mansion was made Changyang Palace.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiashen day the northern residence became Jianzhang Palace and the southern mansion became Changyang Palace.

sentences.zh: 以冠軍將軍邵陵王子元為湘州刺史。

translations.literal: General Who Conquers the Champions Prince Shaoling of Shaoling was made Inspector of Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: General Who Conquers the Champions Prince Shaoling of Shaoling was appointed Inspector of Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 丙戌，原除吳、吳興、義興、晉陵、琅邪五郡大明八年以前逋租。

translations.literal: On bingxu day overdue rents before the eighth year of Daming in Wu, Wuxing, Yixing, Jinling, and Langye—the five commanderies—were remitted.
translations.idiomatic: On the bingxu day overdue rents owed before the eighth year of Daming in the five commanderies of Wu, Wuxing, Yixing, Jinling, and Langye were remitted.

sentences.zh: 己丑，復立南北二馳道。

translations.literal: On jichou day the northern and southern expressways were re-established.
translations.idiomatic: On the jichou day the northern and southern imperial expressways were restored.

sentences.zh: 九月癸巳，車駕幸湖熟，奏鼓吹。

translations.literal: In the ninth month on guisi day the imperial carriage visited Hushu and martial music was performed.
translations.idiomatic: On the guisi day of the ninth month the emperor visited Hushu, where martial music was performed.

sentences.zh: 戊戌，車駕還宮。

translations.literal: On wuxu day the imperial carriage returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: On the wuxu day the emperor returned to the palace.

sentences.zh: 庚子，以南兗州刺史永嘉王子仁為南徐州刺史，丹陽尹始安王子真為南兗州刺史。

translations.literal: On gengzi day Inspector of Southern Yanzhou Prince Yongjia of Yongxing was made Inspector of Southern Xuzhou; Director of Danyang Prince Shi'an of Shi'an was made Inspector of Southern Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On the gengzi day Inspector of Southern Yanzhou Prince Yongjia of Yongxing was reassigned as Inspector of Southern Xuzhou, and Director of Danyang Prince Shi'an of Shi'an was appointed Inspector of Southern Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，撫軍將軍、南徐州刺史新安王子鸞免為庶人，賜死。

translations.literal: On xinchou day General Who Pacifies the Army and Inspector of Southern Xuzhou Prince Xin'an of Xin'an was demoted to commoner status and ordered to die.
translations.idiomatic: On the xinchou day General Who Pacifies the Army and Inspector of Southern Xuzhou Prince Xin'an of Xin'an was stripped of rank, reduced to commoner status, and ordered to take his own life.

sentences.zh: 丙午，以兗州刺史薛安都為平北將軍、徐州刺史。

translations.literal: On bingwu day Inspector of Yanzhou Xue Andu was made General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On the bingwu day Inspector of Yanzhou Xue Andu was appointed General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 丁未，衞將軍湘東王彧加開府儀同三司，特進、右光祿大夫劉遵考為安西將軍、南豫州刺史，寧朔將軍殷孝祖為兗州刺史。

translations.literal: On dingwei day General of the Guard Prince Xiangdong of Xiangdong was given the additional title of Bearer of the Staff with Equal Protocol to a Three-Division Office; Special Grand Master and Right Minister of the Palace Liu Zunkao was made General Who Pacifies the West and Inspector of Southern Yuzhou; General Who Pacifies the Barbarians Yin Xiaozu was made Inspector of Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On the dingwei day General of the Guard Prince Xiangdong of Xiangdong was granted protocol equal to a three-division office; Special Grand Master and Right Minister of the Palace Liu Zunkao became General Who Pacifies the West and Inspector of Southern Yuzhou; and General Who Pacifies the Barbarians Yin Xiaozu was appointed Inspector of Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 戊申，以前梁、南秦二州刺史柳元怙復為梁、南秦二州刺史。

translations.literal: On wushen day former Inspector of Liang and Southern Qin Liu Yuanhu was restored as Inspector of Liang and Southern Qin.
translations.idiomatic: On the wushen day former Inspector of Liang and Southern Qin Liu Yuanhu was reappointed Inspector of Liang and Southern Qin.

sentences.zh: 己酉，車駕討征北將軍、徐州刺史義陽王昶，內外戒嚴。

translations.literal: On jiyou day the imperial carriage campaigned against General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Xuzhou Prince Yiyang of Yiyang; inside and outside the capital martial law was proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiyou day the emperor marched out to attack General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Xuzhou Prince Yiyang of Yiyang, and martial law was proclaimed throughout the capital.

sentences.zh: 昶奔于索虜。

translations.literal: Chang fled to the northern barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: Chang fled to the northern barbarians.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，右將軍、豫州刺史山陽王休祐進號鎮西大將軍。

translations.literal: On xinhai day General of the Right and Inspector of Yuzhou Prince Shanyang of Shanyang was advanced in title to General Who Pacifies the West.
translations.idiomatic: On the xinhai day General of the Right and Inspector of Yuzhou Prince Shanyang of Shanyang was promoted to General Who Pacifies the West.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，以安西長史袁顗為雍州刺史。

translations.literal: On jiayin day Chief Clerk of the Army of the Pacified West Yuan Yi was made Inspector of Yong.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiayin day Chief Clerk of the Army of the Pacified West Yuan Yi was appointed Inspector of Yong.

sentences.zh: 戊午，以左民尚書劉思考為益州刺史。

translations.literal: On wuwu day Director of the Left Household Liu Kaokao was made Inspector of Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: On the wuwu day Director of the Left Household Liu Kaokao was appointed Inspector of Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 是日解嚴，車駕幸瓜步。

translations.literal: That same day martial law was lifted; the imperial carriage visited Guabu.
translations.idiomatic: That same day martial law was lifted and the emperor went to Guabu.

sentences.zh: 開百姓鑄錢。

translations.literal: The common people were permitted to cast coin.
translations.idiomatic: Private casting of coin by the common people was permitted.

sentences.zh: 冬十月癸亥，曲赦徐州。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of winter on guihai day a partial amnesty was proclaimed for Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On the guihai day of the tenth month a partial amnesty was proclaimed for Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 丙寅，車駕還宮。

translations.literal: On bingyin day the imperial carriage returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: On the bingyin day the emperor returned to the palace.

sentences.zh: 以建安王休仁為護軍將軍。

translations.literal: Prince Jian'an of Jian'an was made General Who Protects the Army.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Jian'an of Jian'an was appointed General Who Protects the Army.

sentences.zh: 己卯，東陽太守王藻下獄死。

translations.literal: On jimao day Administrator of Dongyang Wang Zao was imprisoned and died.
translations.idiomatic: On the jimao day Wang Zao, Administrator of Dongyang, was thrown into prison and died there.

sentences.zh: 以宮人謝貴嬪為夫人，加虎賁靸戟，鸞輅龍旂，出警入蹕，實新蔡公主也。

translations.literal: The palace woman Honored Consort Xie was made Lady, given Tiger Guards with halberds, imperial carriage with dragon banners, guards when going out and escort on return—she was in fact Princess Xincai.
translations.idiomatic: The palace woman Honored Consort Xie was elevated to Lady, granted Tiger Guards bearing halberds, an imperial carriage with dragon banners, and full escort on her comings and goings—she was in fact Princess Xincai in disguise.

sentences.zh: 乙酉，以鎮西大將軍、豫州刺史山陽王休祐為鎮軍大將軍、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: On yiyou day General Who Pacifies the West and Inspector of Yuzhou Prince Shanyang of Shanyang was made General Who Pacifies the Army and Bearer of the Staff with Equal Protocol to a Three-Division Office.
translations.idiomatic: On the yiyou day General Who Pacifies the West and Inspector of Yuzhou Prince Shanyang of Shanyang was promoted to General Who Pacifies the Army with protocol equal to a three-division office.

translations.literal: [14] In various editions "General Who Pacifies the West" appears as "General Who Pacifies the North"; on the ninth month xinhai entry and in Xiuyou's biography it reads General Who Pacifies the West, and the text is corrected accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: [Note 14: Various editions read "General Who Pacifies the North" where the received text has "General Who Pacifies the West"; the ninth-month entry and Prince Shanyang's biography support the latter reading.]

sentences.zh: 十一月壬辰，寧朔將軍何邁下獄死。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month on renchen day General Who Pacifies the Barbarians He Mai was imprisoned and died.
translations.idiomatic: On the renchen day of the eleventh month General Who Pacifies the Barbarians He Mai was imprisoned and put to death.

sentences.zh: 新除太尉沈慶之薨。

translations.literal: The newly appointed Grand Commandant Shen Qingzhi died.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Qingzhi, who had just been appointed Grand Commandant, died.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，立皇后路氏，四廂奏樂。

translations.literal: On renyin day Empress Lu was installed; music was performed in all four side chambers.
translations.idiomatic: On the renyin day Empress Lu was installed, with music performed in all four side chambers of the palace.

sentences.zh: 赦揚、南徐二州。

translations.literal: Yang and Southern Xuzhou were granted amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: An amnesty was proclaimed for Yang and Southern Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 護軍將軍建安王休仁加特進、左光祿大夫。

translations.literal: General Who Protects the Army Prince Jian'an of Jian'an was given the additional title of Special Grand Master and Left Minister of the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: General Who Protects the Army Prince Jian'an of Jian'an was further promoted to Special Grand Master and Left Minister of the Palace.

sentences.zh: 中護軍桂陽王休範遷職。

translations.literal: Colonel of the Guard Prince Guiyang of Guiyang was transferred to another post.
translations.idiomatic: Colonel of the Guard Prince Guiyang of Guiyang was reassigned.

sentences.zh: 丁未，皇子生，少府劉勝之子也。

translations.literal: On dingwei day a prince was born—the son of Director of the Palace Treasury Liu Sheng.
translations.idiomatic: On the dingwei day a prince was born, the son of Director of the Palace Treasury Liu Sheng.

sentences.zh: [15]大赦天下。

translations.literal: [15] A general amnesty was proclaimed throughout the empire.
translations.idiomatic: [15] A general amnesty was proclaimed throughout the empire.

sentences.zh: 贓汙淫盜，悉皆原除。

translations.literal: Corruption, licentiousness, and theft were all remitted.
translations.idiomatic: Offenses of corruption, licentiousness, and theft were all pardoned.

sentences.zh: 賜為父後者爵一級。

translations.literal: Those who became heirs for their fathers were granted one rank in nobility.
translations.idiomatic: Those who had become heirs for their fathers were granted one step in noble rank.

sentences.zh: 壬子，以特進、左光祿大夫、護軍將軍建安王休仁為驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: On renzi day Special Grand Master and Left Minister of the Palace and General Who Protects the Army Prince Jian'an of Jian'an was made General-in-Chief Who Runs Fast and Bearer of the Staff with Equal Protocol to a Three-Division Office.
translations.idiomatic: On the renzi day Special Grand Master, Left Minister of the Palace, and General Who Protects the Army Prince Jian'an of Jian'an was appointed General-in-Chief Who Runs Fast with protocol equal to a three-division office.

sentences.zh: 戊午，南平王敬猷、廬陵王敬先、安南侯敬淵並賜死。

translations.literal: On wuwu day Prince Jingyou of Nanping, Prince Jingxian of Luling, and Marquis Jingyuan of Annan were all ordered to die.
translations.idiomatic: On the wuwu day Prince Jingyou of Nanping, Prince Jingxian of Luling, and Marquis Jingyuan of Annan were all ordered to take their own lives.

sentences.zh: 時帝凶悖日甚，誅殺相繼，內外百司，不保首領。

translations.literal: At this time the Emperor's ferocity and perversity grew daily worse; executions followed one after another, and within and without the hundred offices none could be sure of keeping his head.
translations.idiomatic: By then the Emperor's cruelty and perversity were growing worse by the day. Executions followed one after another, and throughout the bureaucracy no one could be sure of keeping his head.

sentences.zh: 先是訛言云：「湘中出天子。

translations.literal: Earlier a false report had said: "A Son of Heaven will arise in Xiang."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier a rumor had spread: "A Son of Heaven will arise in Xiang."

sentences.zh: 」帝將南巡荊、湘二州以厭之。

translations.literal: " The Emperor intended to tour Jing and Xiang to suppress it.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor planned a southern tour of Jing and Xiang to counter the omen.

sentences.zh: 先欲誅諸叔，然後發引。

translations.literal: He first wished to execute his uncles, then set out on the journey.
translations.idiomatic: He intended first to execute his uncles, then set out on the tour.

sentences.zh: 太宗與左右阮佃夫、王道隆、李道兒密結帝左右壽寂之、姜產之等十一人，謀共廢帝。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor secretly joined with his attendants Ruan Tianfu, Wang Daolong, and Li Dao'er to win over the Emperor's attendants Shou Jizhi, Jiang Chanzhi, and eleven others in all, plotting together to depose the Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: The Founding Emperor secretly allied with his confidants Ruan Tianfu, Wang Daolong, and Li Dao'er to win over eleven of the Emperor's attendants, including Shou Jizhi and Jiang Chanzhi, and together they plotted to depose him.

sentences.zh: 戊午夜，帝於華林園竹林堂射鬼。

translations.literal: On the wuwu night the Emperor was at Bamboo Grove Hall in Huangling Garden shooting at ghosts.
translations.idiomatic: At midnight on the wuwu day the Emperor was in Bamboo Grove Hall in Huangling Garden, shooting at ghosts.

sentences.zh: 時巫覡云：「此堂有鬼。

translations.literal: At the time the shamans said: "This hall has ghosts."
translations.idiomatic: The shamans had said, "This hall is haunted."

sentences.zh: 」故帝自射之。

translations.literal: " Therefore the Emperor shot at them himself.
translations.idiomatic: " That was why the Emperor had gone there to shoot at them himself.

sentences.zh: 壽寂之懷刀直入，姜產之為副。

translations.literal: Shou Jizhi entered directly with a knife concealed on his person; Jiang Chanzhi served as his second.
translations.idiomatic: Shou Jizhi entered with a hidden blade; Jiang Chanzhi followed as his second.

sentences.zh: 帝欲走，寂之追而殞之。

translations.literal: The Emperor wished to flee; Jizhi pursued him and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor tried to flee, but Jizhi caught up with him and killed him.

sentences.zh: 時年十七。

translations.literal: He was seventeen years old.
translations.idiomatic: He was seventeen years old.

sentences.zh: 太皇太后令曰：

translations.literal: The Grand Empress Dowager issued an order saying:
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Empress Dowager issued an edict, saying:

sentences.zh: 司徒領護軍八座：子業雖曰嫡長，少稟凶毒，不仁不孝，著自髫齔。

translations.literal: Minister, Colonel of the Garrison, and the Eight Seats: Although Ziye is called the legitimate eldest son, from youth he has borne a fierce and poisonous nature; lack of benevolence and lack of filial piety have been evident since he was but a child.
translations.idiomatic: To the Minister, Colonel of the Garrison, and the Eight Seats: Although Ziye was the legitimate eldest son, from childhood he showed a vicious and poisonous nature; his want of benevolence and filial piety has been plain since he was in his topknot.

sentences.zh: 孝武棄世，屬當辰曆。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu left the world, the time fell to him on the celestial chronology.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu died, the succession fell to him by the calendar of Heaven.

sentences.zh: 自梓宮在殯，喜容靦然，天罰重離，歡恣滋甚。

translations.literal: From the time the imperial coffin lay in mourning, his face was bright and calm; Heaven's punishment of double departure, his wanton joy grew ever greater.
translations.idiomatic: From the moment the late Emperor's coffin lay in state, his face was bright and untroubled; though Heaven had punished the realm with double bereavement, his licentious delight only grew.

sentences.zh: 逼以內外維持，忍虐未露，而凶慘難抑，一旦肆禍，遂縱戮上宰，殄害輔臣。

translations.literal: Compelled by the need to maintain appearances within and without, he restrained his cruelty so it did not show; yet his savage depravity could not be suppressed, and in one morning he unleashed disaster, then wantonly slaughtered the chief ministers and exterminated the assisting ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Outward appearances within and without the court still had to be maintained, so for a time he restrained his cruelty; but his savage depravity could not be held back. In a single morning he unleashed catastrophe, wantonly slaughtering the chief ministers and destroying his chief advisers.

sentences.zh: 子鸞兄弟，先帝鍾愛，含怨既往，枉加屠酷。

translations.literal: Prince Luan and his brothers were beloved of the late Emperor; nursing old resentments, [the Emperor] wrongly added cruel slaughter.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Luan and his brothers had been the late Emperor's favorites; nursing old resentments, the Emperor had them slaughtered without cause.

sentences.zh: 昶茂親作扞，橫相徵討。

translations.literal: Chang, a close kinsman of the imperial clan, served as a shield; yet [the Emperor] recklessly raised troops to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: Chang, a close imperial kinsman, had stood as a bulwark for the house, yet the Emperor raised troops against him without cause.

sentences.zh: 新蔡公主逼離夫族，幽置深宮，詭云薨殞。

translations.literal: Princess Xincai was forced from her husband's clan, hidden deep in the palace, falsely declared to have died.
translations.idiomatic: Princess Xincai was torn from her husband's family, hidden away in the inner palace, and falsely declared dead.

sentences.zh: 襄事甫爾，喪禮頓釋，昏酣長夜，庶事傾遺。

translations.literal: The mourning affair had barely begun when funeral rites were abruptly cast aside; drunk through the long night, all affairs of state were abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: Hardly had mourning begun when funeral observances were cast aside; he drank through the long nights while affairs of state were left in ruins.

sentences.zh: 朝賢舊勳，棄若遺土。

translations.literal: Worthy ministers of long service were discarded like forgotten soil.
translations.idiomatic: Veteran ministers of merit were cast aside like worthless dust.

sentences.zh: 管絃不輟，珍羞備膳。

translations.literal: Pipes and strings never ceased; delicacies filled every meal.
translations.idiomatic: Music never ceased; every meal was heaped with delicacies.

sentences.zh: 詈辱祖考，以為戲謔。

translations.literal: He cursed and insulted his ancestors, taking it as jest and play.
translations.idiomatic: He reviled his ancestors and made a jest of it.

sentences.zh: 行游莫止，淫縱無度。

translations.literal: His travels knew no limit; his licentious excess had no measure.
translations.idiomatic: His wanderings knew no bounds; his licentious excess knew no limit.

sentences.zh: 肆宴園陵，規圖發掘。

translations.literal: He held banquets at the imperial tombs and plotted to excavate them.
translations.idiomatic: He feasted at the imperial tombs and plotted their desecration.

sentences.zh: 誅剪無辜，籍略婦女。

translations.literal: He executed the innocent and seized women by force.
translations.idiomatic: He put the innocent to death and seized women by force.

sentences.zh: 建樹偽豎，莫知誰息。

translations.literal: He raised false heirs, and none knew whose line would breathe on.
translations.idiomatic: He set up false heirs, and no one knew whose line would survive.

sentences.zh: 拜嬪立后，慶過恒典。

translations.literal: In appointing consorts and establishing empresses, his celebrations exceeded the constant statutes.
translations.idiomatic: In elevating consorts and installing an empress, his celebrations exceeded all precedent.

sentences.zh: 宗室密戚，遇若婢僕，鞭捶陵曳，無復尊卑。

translations.literal: Imperial clansmen and close kin were treated like maidservants and menials; flogging, beating, and dragging left no distinction of rank.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial kinsmen and close relatives were treated like servants; flogging, beating, and dragging them about erased every distinction of rank.

sentences.zh: 南平一門，特鍾其酷。

translations.literal: The house of Nanping alone received his cruelty in special measure.
translations.idiomatic: The house of Nanping alone bore the full brunt of his cruelty.

sentences.zh: 反天滅理，顯暴萬端。

translations.literal: Reversing Heaven and extinguishing principle, his open violence had ten thousand forms.
translations.idiomatic: He reversed Heaven and extinguished moral principle; his open violence took ten thousand forms.

sentences.zh: 苛罰酷令，終無紀極，夏桀、殷辛，未足以譬。

translations.literal: Harsh punishments and cruel orders knew no end or limit; Jie of Xia and Xin of Yin would not suffice for comparison.
translations.idiomatic: His harsh punishments and cruel edicts knew no end; even Jie of Xia and Xin of Yin would not suffice for comparison.

sentences.zh: 闔朝業業，人不自保，百姓遑遑，手足靡厝。

translations.literal: The whole court was fearful; men could not preserve themselves; the common people were anxious, their hands and feet with no place to rest.
translations.idiomatic: The whole court trembled; no official could feel safe; the people lived in dread, with nowhere to set hand or foot.

sentences.zh: 行穢禽獸，罪盈三千。

translations.literal: His conduct was filthy as a beast's; his crimes filled the three thousand categories.
translations.idiomatic: His conduct was filthier than a beast's; his crimes filled every category of the law.

sentences.zh: 高祖之業將泯，七廟之享幾絕。

translations.literal: The enterprise of the High Ancestor was about to perish; the sacrifices of the seven temples nearly cut off.
translations.idiomatic: The founding emperor's legacy was on the verge of extinction; the sacrifices of the seven temples nearly came to an end.

sentences.zh: 吾老疾沈篤，每規禍鴆，憂煎漏刻，氣命無幾。

translations.literal: I am old and my illness deep; daily I foresee the poisoned cup; worry burns through each water-clock mark, and my breath and life have not long to run.
translations.idiomatic: I am aged and gravely ill; day after day I foresee disaster; anxiety consumes me hour by hour, and my life has not long to run.

sentences.zh: 開闢以降，所未嘗聞。

translations.literal: Since the opening of the age, nothing like this has been heard.
translations.idiomatic: Since the dynasty was founded, nothing like this has been heard of.

sentences.zh: 遠近思奮，十室而九。

translations.literal: Near and far yearn to rise up; nine houses in ten.
translations.idiomatic: Near and far the people yearn to rise against him; nine households in ten.

sentences.zh: 衞將軍湘東王體自太祖，天縱英聖，文皇鍾愛，寵冠列藩。

translations.literal: General of the Guard Prince Xiangdong of Xiangdong derives his person from the Great Ancestor; Heaven endowed him with heroic sagacity; Emperor Wen cherished him, his favor surpassing all the feudatories.
translations.idiomatic: General of the Guard Prince Xiangdong of Xiangdong is descended from the Great Ancestor; Heaven endowed him with heroic sagacity; Emperor Wen cherished him above all the feudal princes.

sentences.zh: 吾早識神睿，特兼常禮。

translations.literal: I early recognized his divine keenness and treated him with special courtesy beyond the ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: I recognized his brilliance early and treated him with honors beyond the ordinary.

sentences.zh: 潛運宏規，義士投袂，獨夫既殞，懸首白旗，社稷再興，宗祏永固，人鬼屬心，大命允集。

translations.literal: He secretly carried out a great design; men of righteousness flung aside their sleeves; the tyrant has now fallen, his head hung from the white banner; the altars of state rise again, the ancestral temple stands firm forever; men and spirits turn their hearts to him; the great mandate is truly gathered.
translations.idiomatic: He carried out his great design in secret; men of righteousness rose up; the tyrant has fallen, his head displayed on the white banner; the altars of state are restored, the ancestral temple secured; men and spirits alike turn to him; the great mandate is truly his.

sentences.zh: 且勳德高邈，大業攸歸，宜遵漢、晉，纂承皇極。

translations.literal: Moreover his merit and virtue are lofty and far-reaching; the great enterprise returns to him; it is fitting to follow Han and Jin in succeeding to the imperial apex.
translations.idiomatic: His merit and virtue are lofty; the great enterprise belongs to him; he should follow the precedents of Han and Jin in ascending the throne.

sentences.zh: 主者詳舊典以時奉行。

translations.literal: Let those in charge examine the old statutes and carry them out in timely fashion.
translations.idiomatic: Let the responsible offices examine the old statutes and carry them out without delay.

sentences.zh: 未亡人餘年不幸嬰此百艱，永尋情事，雖存若殞。

translations.literal: This surviving remnant of years has unhappily encountered this hundredfold calamity; forever recalling the circumstances, though alive I am as if dead.
translations.idiomatic: In my remaining years I have met this hundredfold calamity; whenever I recall what has happened, I am as good as dead though I still live.

sentences.zh: 當復奈何！

translations.literal: What is to be done! What is to be done!
translations.idiomatic: What is to be done! What is to be done!

sentences.zh: 當復奈何！

translations.literal: What is to be done! What is to be done!
translations.idiomatic: What is to be done! What is to be done!

sentences.zh: 葬廢帝丹陽秣陵縣南郊壇西。

translations.literal: The deposed Emperor was buried west of the southern suburban altar in Moling county, Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: The deposed Emperor was buried west of the southern suburban altar in Moling county, Danyang.

sentences.zh: 帝幼而狷急，在東宮每為世祖所責。

translations.literal: The Emperor from youth was narrow and impatient; in the Eastern Palace he was often rebuked by the Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: From childhood the Emperor was narrow and quick-tempered; in the Eastern Palace he was often rebuked by his father.

sentences.zh: 世祖西巡，子業啟參承起居，書迹不謹，上詰讓之。

translations.literal: When the Emperor toured the west, Ziye submitted memorials reporting on his daily health; his handwriting was careless, and the Emperor questioned and reproached him.
translations.idiomatic: When his father toured the west, Ziye sent memorials reporting on court routine; his handwriting was careless, and the Emperor questioned and reproached him.

sentences.zh: 子業啟事陳謝，上又答曰：「書不長進，此是一條耳。

translations.literal: Ziye submitted a memorial expressing apology; the Emperor again replied: "Your writing does not improve—this is one matter alone.
translations.idiomatic: Ziye submitted a memorial of apology; the Emperor replied again: "Your writing shows no improvement—that is one fault among many.

sentences.zh: 聞汝素都懈怠，狷戾日甚，何以頑固乃爾邪！

translations.literal: I hear you have always been idle and lax, and your perversity grows worse day by day—how can you be so stubborn!"
translations.idiomatic: I hear you have always been idle and lax, and your perversity grows worse by the day—how can you be so obstinate!"

sentences.zh: 」初踐阼，受璽紱，悖然無哀容。

translations.literal: " When he first ascended the throne and received the seal and ribbon, his manner was perverse and without mourning expression.
translations.idiomatic: " When he first took the throne and received the imperial seal and ribbon, his face showed no grief.

sentences.zh: 始猶難諸大臣及戴法興等，既殺法興，諸大臣莫不震懾。

translations.literal: At first he still found the great ministers and Dai Faxing and others difficult; after Faxing was killed, none of the great ministers was not shaken with fear.
translations.idiomatic: At first he still found the senior ministers and Dai Faxing hard to control; once Faxing was killed, every senior minister trembled with fear.

sentences.zh: 於是又誅羣公。

translations.literal: Then he again executed the host of dukes.
translations.idiomatic: Then he turned to slaughter the great nobles as well.

sentences.zh: 元凱以下，皆被毆捶牽曳。

translations.literal: From Yuan Kai downward, all were beaten, flogged, and dragged about.
translations.idiomatic: From Yuan Kai downward, all were beaten, flogged, and dragged about the palace.

sentences.zh: 內外危懼，殿省騷然。

translations.literal: Within and without there was peril and fear; the palace offices were in uproar.
translations.idiomatic: Inside and outside the palace there was terror; the offices were in uproar.

sentences.zh: 初太后疾篤，遣呼帝。

translations.literal: When the Empress Dowager first fell gravely ill, she sent to summon the Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: When the Empress Dowager first fell gravely ill, she sent for the Emperor.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「病人間多鬼，可畏，那可往。

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "Sickrooms have many ghosts—it is fearful; how could one go there?"
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "Sickrooms are full of ghosts—it is terrifying. How could I go there?"

sentences.zh: 」太后怒，語侍者：「將刀來，破我腹，那得生如此寧馨兒！

translations.literal: " The Empress Dowager in anger told her attendants: "Bring a knife and cut open my belly—how could I have borne such a precious little darling!"
translations.idiomatic: " In anger the Empress Dowager told her attendants, "Bring a knife and cut open my belly—how could I have given birth to such a precious little monster!"

sentences.zh: 」及太后崩後數日，帝夢太后謂之曰：「汝不孝不仁，本無人君之相。

translations.literal: " Several days after the Empress Dowager died, the Emperor dreamed the Empress Dowager said to him: "You are unfilial and unkind; originally you had no aspect of a ruler of men.
translations.idiomatic: " A few days after the Empress Dowager died, the Emperor dreamed that she said to him, "You are unfilial and unkind; you never had the bearing of a ruler.

sentences.zh: 子尚愚悖如此，亦非運祚所及。

translations.literal: Zishang is so foolish and perverse that he too is not within the span of fortune's mandate.
translations.idiomatic: Zishang is as foolish and perverse as you; he too lies outside the mandate of fortune.

sentences.zh: 孝武險虐滅道，怨結人神，兒子雖多，並無天命。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowu was dangerous and cruel, extinguishing the Way; resentment bound men and spirits; though his sons were many, none had Heaven's mandate.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowu was violent and cruel and turned his back on the Way; his deeds bound men and spirits in resentment; though he had many sons, none possessed Heaven's mandate.

sentences.zh: 大運所歸，應還文帝之子。

translations.literal: The great turn of fortune returns; it should go back to a son of Emperor Wen."
translations.idiomatic: The great turn of fortune belongs elsewhere: it should return to a son of Emperor Wen."

sentences.zh: 」其後湘東王紹位，果文帝子也。

translations.literal: Afterward Prince Xiangdong of Xiangdong succeeded to the throne, and he was indeed a son of Emperor Wen.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Xiangdong of Xiangdong later took the throne, he was indeed a son of Emperor Wen.

sentences.zh: 故帝聚諸叔京邑，慮在外為患。

translations.literal: Therefore the Emperor gathered his uncles in the capital, fearing they would become a threat outside.
translations.idiomatic: For that reason the Emperor gathered his uncles in the capital, fearing trouble if they remained in the provinces.

sentences.zh: 山陰公主淫恣過度，謂帝曰：「妾與陛下，雖男女有殊，俱託體先帝。

translations.literal: The Princess of Shanyin was licentious beyond measure and said to the Emperor: "Your servant and Your Majesty, though male and female differ, both owe our bodies to the late Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: The Princess of Shanyin was extravagantly licentious and said to the Emperor, "Your Majesty and I, though man and woman differ, both owe our bodies to the late Emperor.

sentences.zh: 陛下六宮萬數，而妾唯駙馬一人。

translations.literal: Your Majesty has ten thousand women in the six palaces, while your servant has only one husband.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has ten thousand consorts in the six palaces, while I have only one husband.

sentences.zh: 事不均平，一何至此！

translations.literal: The affair is so unequal—how can it have come to this!"
translations.idiomatic: The disparity is outrageous—how did it come to this!"

sentences.zh: 」帝乃為主置面首左右三十人；

translations.literal: " The Emperor then set up thirty male favorites on her left and right;
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor then provided her with thirty male companions at court;

sentences.zh: 進爵會稽郡長公主，秩同郡王，食湯沐邑二千戶，[16]給鼓吹一部，加班劍二十人。

translations.literal: her rank was advanced to Grand Princess of Kuaiji commandery, equal in rank to a prince of a commandery, with a fief of two thousand households for bathing and maintenance, [16] one set of martial music granted, and twenty men with ceremonial swords added.
translations.idiomatic: she was advanced to Grand Princess of Kuaiji with rank equal to a commandery prince, granted a maintenance fief of two thousand households, [16] given a full set of martial music, and assigned twenty ceremonial sword bearers.

sentences.zh: 帝每出，與朝臣常共陪輦。

translations.literal: Whenever the Emperor went out, he commonly shared the imperial carriage with court ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the Emperor went out, court ministers commonly shared his carriage.

sentences.zh: 主以吏部郎褚淵貌美，就帝請以自侍，帝許之。

translations.literal: The Princess, finding Director of the Ministry of Personnel Chu Yuan handsome, asked the Emperor that he serve her; the Emperor consented.
translations.idiomatic: The Princess, finding Director of the Ministry of Personnel Chu Yuan handsome, asked the Emperor to let him attend her; the Emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 淵侍主十日，備見逼迫，誓死不回，遂得免。

translations.literal: Yuan attended the Princess for ten days, was fully subjected to coercion, vowed to die rather than yield, and thus was released.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan attended her for ten days under relentless pressure, swore he would rather die than submit, and was finally released.

sentences.zh: 帝所幸閹人華願兒，官至散騎常侍，加將軍帶郡。

translations.literal: The eunuch Hua Yuan'er, whom the Emperor favored, reached Attendant at the Palace Gate and was given the additional title of general with a commandery.
translations.idiomatic: The favored eunuch Hua Yuan'er rose to Attendant at the Palace Gate and was further made a general with a nominal commandery.

sentences.zh: 帝少好讀書，[17]頗識古事，自造世祖誄及雜篇章，往往有辭采。

translations.literal: The Emperor from youth loved reading books, [17] was quite versed in ancient matters, himself composed the eulogy for the Emperor and miscellaneous pieces, which often had literary color.
translations.idiomatic: In youth the Emperor loved reading, [17] knew antiquity well, and composed his father's eulogy and other pieces that often showed real literary grace.

sentences.zh: 以魏武帝有發丘中郎將、摸金校尉，乃置此二官。

translations.literal: Because Emperor Wu of Wei had the office of Director of Tomb Opening and Colonel Who Searches for Gold, he established these two offices.
translations.idiomatic: Because Emperor Wu of Wei had created the offices of Director of Tomb Opening and Colonel Who Searches for Gold, he established these two posts as well.

sentences.zh: 以建安王休仁、山陽王休祐領之。

translations.literal: Prince Jian'an of Jian'an and Prince Shanyang of Shanyang were placed in charge of them.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Jian'an of Jian'an and Prince Shanyang of Shanyang were put in charge of them.

sentences.zh: [18]其餘事迹，分見諸列傳。

translations.literal: [18] His remaining deeds are set forth separately in the various biographies.
translations.idiomatic: [Note 18: His remaining deeds are treated separately in the various biographical chapters.]

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：廢帝之事行著于篇。

translations.literal: The historian says: The deeds of the deposed Emperor are set forth in this chapter.
translations.idiomatic: The historian comments: The deeds of the deposed Emperor are set forth in this chapter.

sentences.zh: 若夫武王數殷紂之釁，不能絓其萬一；

translations.literal: As for King Wu numbering the offenses of Zhou of Yin, he could not exhaust one part in ten thousand;
translations.idiomatic: When King Wu counted the crimes of King Zhou of Yin, he could not exhaust one part in ten thousand;

sentences.zh: 霍光書昌邑之過，未足舉其毫釐。

translations.literal: Huo Guang wrote the faults of the Marquis of Changyi, yet could not raise one hair's breadth of them.
translations.idiomatic: when Huo Guang recorded the faults of the Marquis of Changyi, he could not capture one hair's breadth of them.

sentences.zh: 假以中才之君，有一于此，足以霣社殘宗，汚宮瀦廟，況總斯惡以萃一人之體乎！

translations.literal: Suppose an emperor of middling talent had one of these—it would suffice to topple the altars and ruin the clan, defile the palace and flood the temple; how much more when all these evils were gathered in a single person's body!
translations.idiomatic: A ruler of merely middling talent who committed even one such act would suffice to topple the altars, ruin his house, and defile the ancestral temple—how much more when every evil was gathered in a single man!

sentences.zh: 其得亡亦為幸矣。

translations.literal: That he escaped destruction was also a piece of fortune.
translations.idiomatic: That the dynasty survived his reign at all was itself a kind of fortune.

sentences.zh: 校勘記

translations.literal: Textual collation notes
translations.idiomatic: Textual collation notes

sentences.zh: 出居東宮 各本並脫「居」字，據元龜二五六補。

translations.literal: Moved out to reside in the Eastern Palace: all editions omit the character "reside"; supplied from Yuan Gui 256.
translations.idiomatic: Moved out to reside in the Eastern Palace: all editions omit the character "reside"; supplied from Yuan Gui 256.

sentences.zh: 丹陽尹永嘉王子仁為南豫州刺史 「南豫」子仁傳作「南兗」。

translations.literal: Director of Danyang Prince Yongjia of Yongxing was made Inspector of Southern Yuzhou: in Ziren's biography the post reads Southern Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Director of Danyang Prince Yongjia of Yongxing was made Inspector of Southern Yuzhou: in Ziren's biography the post reads Southern Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 繁而傷治 「傷」各本並作「作」，據元龜一九一改。

translations.literal: Elaborate and harmful to governance: in all editions "harmful" reads "made"; changed according to Yuan Gui 19.
translations.idiomatic: Elaborate and harmful to governance: in all editions "harmful" reads "made"; changed according to Yuan Gui 19.

sentences.zh: 氣緯舛互 「互」各本並作「玄」，蓋形近而譌，今改正。

translations.literal: The qi configurations cross and conflict: in all editions "conflict" reads "mysterious"; likely a graphic error near "conflict," and the text is corrected accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: The qi configurations cross and conflict: in all editions "conflict" reads "mysterious"; likely a graphic error near "conflict," and the text is corrected accordingly.

sentences.zh: 領軍將軍王玄謨為鎮北將軍青冀二州刺史 各本「鎮北將軍」下並衍「南徐州刺史新安王子鸞為」十一字。

translations.literal: Colonel of the Garrison Wang Xuemo was made General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Qing and Ji: below "General Who Pacifies the North" all editions interpolate the eleven characters "Inspector of Southern Xuzhou Prince Xin'an of Xin'an was."
translations.idiomatic: Colonel of the Garrison Wang Xuemo was made General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Qing and Ji: below "General Who Pacifies the North" all editions interpolate the eleven characters "Inspector of Southern Xuzhou Prince Xin'an of Xin'an was."

sentences.zh: 按新安王子鸞傳，不言曾為青、冀二州刺史，而王玄謨傳，言玄謨時徙為青、冀二州刺史。

translations.literal: According to the biography of Prince Xin'an of Xin'an, it is not stated that he ever served as Inspector of Qing and Ji, whereas in Wang Xuemo's biography it says Xuemo was at that time transferred to Inspector of Qing and Ji.
translations.idiomatic: According to the biography of Prince Xin'an of Xin'an, it is not stated that he ever served as Inspector of Qing and Ji, whereas in Wang Xuemo's biography it says Xuemo was at that time transferred to Inspector of Qing and Ji.

sentences.zh: 今訂正。

translations.literal: The text is now corrected.
translations.idiomatic: The text is now corrected.

sentences.zh: 己丑 各本並作「己未」。

translations.literal: On jichou day: in all editions the day reads jiwei.
translations.idiomatic: On jichou day: in all editions the day reads jiwei.

sentences.zh: 按是月丁卯朔，二十三日己丑，無己未、乙丑。

translations.literal: According to the calendar, that month began on dingmao; the twenty-third day is jichou—there is no jiwei or yichou.
translations.idiomatic: According to the calendar, that month began on dingmao; the twenty-third day is jichou—there is no jiwei or yichou.

sentences.zh: 今據建康實錄及通鑑改正。

translations.literal: Now corrected according to the Jiankang shilu and Zizhi tongjian.
translations.idiomatic: Now corrected according to the Jiankang shilu and Zizhi tongjian.

sentences.zh: 庚寅 各本並作「庚子」。

translations.literal: On gengyin day: in all editions the day reads gengzi.
translations.idiomatic: On gengyin day: in all editions the day reads gengzi.

sentences.zh: 按是月丁卯朔，無庚子，二十三日己丑後，二十四日有庚寅。

translations.literal: According to the calendar, that month began on dingmao; there is no gengzi; after the twenty-third day jichou, the twenty-fourth day is gengyin.
translations.idiomatic: According to the calendar, that month began on dingmao; there is no gengzi; after the twenty-third day jichou, the twenty-fourth day is gengyin.

sentences.zh: 今改正。

translations.literal: Now corrected.
translations.idiomatic: Now corrected.

sentences.zh: 輔國將軍宗越為司州刺史 「宗越」書中多誤作「宋越」，今據宗越傳改正。

translations.literal: General Who Assists the State Zong Yue was made Inspector of Sizhou: in the book "Zong Yue" is often written wrongly as "Song Yue"; now corrected according to the biography of Zong Yue.
translations.idiomatic: General Who Assists the State Zong Yue was made Inspector of Sizhou: in the book "Zong Yue" is often written wrongly as "Song Yue"; now corrected according to the biography of Zong Yue.

sentences.zh: 以下類此者皆逕改，不具校。

translations.literal: Below, similar cases are all corrected directly without separate collation.
translations.idiomatic: Below, similar cases are all corrected directly without separate collation.

sentences.zh: 以尚書右僕射顏師伯為尚書僕射 「尚書僕射」各本作「尚書左僕射」，南史無「左」字。

translations.literal: Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Yan Shibo was made Vice Director of the Masters of Writing: in all editions "Vice Director" reads "Left Vice Director"; the Nan shi has no character "left."
translations.idiomatic: Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Yan Shibo was made Vice Director of the Masters of Writing: in all editions "Vice Director" reads "Left Vice Director"; the Nan shi has no character "left."

sentences.zh: 李慈銘宋書札記云：「左字衍，當據南史刪。

translations.literal: Li Ciming's notes on the Song shu say: "The character left is an interpolation and should be deleted according to the Nan shi."
translations.idiomatic: Li Ciming's notes on the Song shu say: "The character left is an interpolation and should be deleted according to the Nan shi."

sentences.zh: 」按是時但置尚書僕射，不分立左右。

translations.literal: " According to this, at the time only Vice Director of the Masters of Writing was established, without separate left and right posts.
translations.idiomatic: " At that time only a single Vice Director of the Masters of Writing was appointed, without separate left and right posts.

sentences.zh: 今據南史刪「左」字。

translations.literal: Now the character "left" is deleted according to the Nan shi.
translations.idiomatic: Now the character "left" is deleted according to the Nan shi.

sentences.zh: 減州郡縣田祿之半 宋本、三朝本、北監本、毛本及南史作「田祿」。

translations.literal: Reduced by half the field salaries of provinces, commanderies, and counties: the Song edition, Three Dynasties edition, Northern Directorate edition, Mao edition, and Nan shi read "field salaries."
translations.idiomatic: Reduced by half the field salaries of provinces, commanderies, and counties: the Song edition, Three Dynasties edition, Northern Directorate edition, Mao edition, and Nan shi read "field salaries."

sentences.zh: 殿本、局本作「田租」。

translations.literal: The Hall edition and Bureau edition read "field tax."
translations.idiomatic: The Hall edition and Bureau edition read "field tax."

sentences.zh: 建康實錄作「祿秩」。

translations.literal: The Jiankang shilu reads "salary ranks."
translations.idiomatic: The Jiankang shilu reads "salary ranks."

sentences.zh: 按普減國內田租之半，非封建統治者所肯為，此必減州郡縣官吏田祿之半。

translations.literal: According to this, a general reduction of the empire's field tax by half is not something a feudal ruler would undertake; this must mean reducing by half the field salaries of officials in provinces, commanderies, and counties.
translations.idiomatic: A general halving of land tax throughout the realm is not something a feudal ruler would undertake; the passage must refer to halving the field-salary allotments of officials in provinces, commanderies, and counties.

sentences.zh: 故建康實錄改稱為「祿秩」。

translations.literal: Therefore the Jiankang shilu changed the wording to "salary ranks."
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the Jiankang shilu changed the wording to "salary ranks."

sentences.zh: 衞將軍南豫州刺史湘東王彧改為雍州刺史 各本並脫「南」字。

translations.literal: General of the Guard and Inspector of Southern Yuzhou Prince Xiangdong of Xiangdong was changed to Inspector of Yong: all editions omit the character "south."
translations.idiomatic: General of the Guard and Inspector of Southern Yuzhou Prince Xiangdong of Xiangdong was changed to Inspector of Yong: all editions omit the character "south."

sentences.zh: 按明帝紀，永光元年為南豫州刺史，鎮姑孰。

translations.literal: According to the annals of Emperor Ming, in the first year of Yongguang he was Inspector of Southern Yuzhou, garrisoning Gushu.
translations.idiomatic: According to the annals of Emperor Ming, in the first year of Yongguang he was Inspector of Southern Yuzhou, garrisoning Gushu.

sentences.zh: 又按州郡志，此時南豫州鎮姑孰，而豫州則未嘗以姑孰為州治。

translations.literal: Moreover, according to the gazetteer of provinces and commanderies, at this time Southern Yuzhou was garrisoned at Gushu, whereas Yuzhou had never used Gushu as its seat.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, according to the gazetteer of provinces and commanderies, at this time Southern Yuzhou was garrisoned at Gushu, whereas Yuzhou had never used Gushu as its seat.

sentences.zh: 今據明帝紀補。

translations.literal: Now supplied according to the annals of Emperor Ming.
translations.idiomatic: Now supplied according to the annals of Emperor Ming.

sentences.zh: 尚書左僕射顏師伯 「尚書左僕射」各本並作「尚書僕射」，據南史改，說見前。

translations.literal: Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Yan Shibo: in all editions "Left Vice Director" reads "Vice Director"; changed according to the Nan shi, as explained above.
translations.idiomatic: Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Yan Shibo: in all editions "Left Vice Director" reads "Vice Director"; changed according to the Nan shi, as explained above.

sentences.zh: 以鎮西大將軍豫州刺史山陽王休祐為鎮軍大將軍開府儀同三司 鎮西大將軍各本並作「鎮北大將軍」。

translations.literal: General Who Pacifies the West and Inspector of Yuzhou Prince Shanyang of Shanyang was made General Who Pacifies the Army and Bearer of the Staff with Equal Protocol to a Three-Division Office: in all editions "General Who Pacifies the West" reads "General Who Pacifies the North."
translations.idiomatic: General Who Pacifies the West and Inspector of Yuzhou Prince Shanyang of Shanyang was made General Who Pacifies the Army and Bearer of the Staff with Equal Protocol to a Three-Division Office: in all editions "General Who Pacifies the West" reads "General Who Pacifies the North."

sentences.zh: 上九月辛亥下作鎮西大將軍，休祐傳亦作鎮西，今改正。

translations.literal: Above, in the ninth month on xinhai day it reads General Who Pacifies the West, and Xiuyou's biography also reads General Who Pacifies the West; now corrected.
translations.idiomatic: Above, in the ninth month on xinhai day it reads General Who Pacifies the West, and Xiuyou's biography also reads General Who Pacifies the West; now corrected.

sentences.zh: 少府劉勝之子也 「劉勝」元龜一九七及二０七同本紀。

translations.literal: The son of Director of the Palace Treasury Liu Sheng: "Liu Sheng" appears thus in Yuan Gui 197 and 207 in the same annals.
translations.idiomatic: The son of Director of the Palace Treasury Liu Sheng: "Liu Sheng" appears thus in Yuan Gui 197 and 207 in the same annals.

sentences.zh: 符瑞志及始安王休仁傳、宋略、南史帝紀作劉矇，南史休仁傳作劉蒙。

translations.literal: The Treatise on Omens, the biography of Prince Shi'an of Shi'an, the Song lüe, and the annals in the Nan shi write Liu Meng; the biography of Xiuren in the Nan shi writes Liu Meng.
translations.idiomatic: The Treatise on Omens, the biography of Prince Shi'an of Shi'an, the Song lüe, and the annals in the Nan shi write Liu Meng; the biography of Xiuren in the Nan shi writes Liu Meng.

sentences.zh: 食湯沐邑二千戶 「食」各本並作「侯」。

translations.literal: Granted a fief of two thousand households for bathing and maintenance: in all editions "granted" reads "marquis."
translations.idiomatic: Granted a fief of two thousand households for bathing and maintenance: in all editions "granted" reads "marquis."

sentences.zh: 據御覽一五二改。

translations.literal: Changed according to the Imperial Readings 152.
translations.idiomatic: Changed according to the Imperial Readings 152.

sentences.zh: 帝少好讀書 「讀書」各本並作「講書」，據南史、元龜一九二、御覽一二八引改。

translations.literal: The Emperor from youth loved reading books: in all editions "reading books" reads "lecturing on books"; changed according to the Nan shi, Yuan Gui 192, and the citation in Imperial Readings 128.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor from youth loved reading books: in all editions "reading books" reads "lecturing on books"; changed according to the Nan shi, Yuan Gui 192, and the citation in Imperial Readings 128.

sentences.zh: 以建安王休仁山陽王休祐領之 各本並脫「休仁山陽王」五字，據南史補。

translations.literal: Prince Jian'an of Jian'an and Prince Shanyang of Shanyang were placed in charge of them: all editions omit the five characters "Xiuren Prince Shanyang."
translations.idiomatic: Prince Jian'an of Jian'an and Prince Shanyang of Shanyang were placed in charge of them: all editions omit the five characters "Xiuren Prince Shanyang."

sentences.zh: 張燴讀史舉正云：「按建安王乃休仁，休祐則山陽王也。

translations.literal: Zhang Hui's Corrections in Reading History says: "According to this, Prince Jian'an is Xiuren, and Xiuyou is Prince Shanyang."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Hui's Corrections in Reading History says: "According to this, Prince Jian'an is Xiuren, and Xiuyou is Prince Shanyang."

sentences.zh: 南史作『以建安王休仁、山陽王休祐領之』為是。」

translations.literal: The Nan shi reading "Prince Jian'an of Jian'an and Prince Shanyang of Shanyang were placed in charge of them" is correct."
translations.idiomatic: The Nan shi reading "Prince Jian'an of Jian'an and Prince Shanyang of Shanyang were placed in charge of them" is correct."
